items.title: John Cena Reveals the Touching Reason Why Warner Bros.’ Initial Decision to Shelve Coyote vs Acme Didn’t Devastate Him
items.description: John Cena opened up about the graceful way he handled Warner Bros.’ infamously unpopular decision to shelve Coyote vs Acme back in 2023 and how James Gunn’s influence on the film still lingers.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
John Cena opened up about the graceful way he handled Warner Bros.’ infamously unpopular decision to shelve Coyote vs Acme back in 2023 and how James Gunn’s influence on the film still lingers.

Coyote vs Acme is finally headed toward its long-awaited theatrical release on August 28, 2026. It’s been a years-long battle to get it on the silver screen after Warner Bros. shelved the project, originally intended as a Max streaming exclusive, in favor of focusing on feature films with cinema showings.

Things are finally back on track, but it took a lot of doing. Thanks to fan outcry and an industry campaign, Coyote vs Acme is getting the Hollywood treatment it deserves, and it’s already being met with rave reviews.

IGN’s Tom Jorgensen got the chance to sit down with the film’s cast prior to its August 28 release, where he asked if there were any particular moments from the film they’d be disappointed would never see the light of day back when the project got shuttered.

While cast members like Will Forte expressed some sadness about not being able to watch the film with his children, John Cena had a decidedly different approach to managing his emotions around the setback.

“I’m not sure I look at it like that,” Cena said. “Rather than look at any experience of life like, ‘If only,’ I was very grateful to have worked with these two, to have been directed to become a better performer, to make friends along the way. I just choose not to look at it like that. Because all that stuff, all that kerfuffle is so far beyond my reach and control.”

“I think what we hope to do is carry the torch and carry the flame for these characters the best we can,” director Dave Green added. “Because we are just temporary custodians of this historic, legacy IP. It’s just an honor to be able to play in that sandbox at all. I was kind of feeling like, ‘It’s too bad that kids won’t be able to grow up on a new iteration of Looney Tunes that hopefully carries that legacy tone and voice.’ But hey, we're sitting here with you today. It worked out.”

The group also discussed James Gunn’s lasting impact on the movie. Gunn pitched the project over a decade ago, co-writing the story and even bringing in John Cena to star after personally recommending the script to him.

Cena referenced the famous article written by Ian Frazier for The New Yorker magazine back in 1990, which ultimately inspired the movie. It was a humorous, satirical piece that outlined a fake lawsuit against Acme on Wile E. Coyote’s behalf.

“It is on the square,” Cena said of Gunn’s narrative flair. “I think James takes the outlandish and leans into the straightness of it. The article was written of, ‘What if.’ Like, ‘Hey, for 75 years we’ve been watching this wrong?’ And that’s like, ‘Oh my god, I have.’ That’s James Gunn. He’s a guy who will take the picture on the wall, and turn it like that, and you’ll be like, ‘What?’ …I know and love James, and from the time we shared, that’s him.”

Coyote vs Acme is shaping up to be one of the best-received films of the year, debuting on Rotten Tomatoes with a 100% score. IGN’s Clint Gage gave it a 9 out of 10, saying the movie “shows why Looney Tunes are just as funny now as they’ve ever been, with a film that’s an amazingly meta answer to corporate shenanigans.”

Image Credits: Michael Buckner/Variety via Getty Images

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

items.title: Xbox Special Edition Translucent Green Controller Price, Release Date Leaked
items.description: Pricing and launch details for Microsoft's snazzy translucent green Xbox controller have leaked online.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Pricing and launch details for Microsoft's snazzy translucent green Xbox controller have leaked online.

Inspired by the iconic OG Xbox console, the Xbox Wireless Controller Special Edition X25 will launch on October 20, 2026 priced at $79.99 / £74.99 / €79.99, according to Dealabs' ever-reliable billbil-kun.

Microsoft will reportedly make these details official next week at Gamescom in Cologne, Germany, with preorders set to go live on August 26. As yet, however, there's no word on the X25 Special Edition Xbox Series X — or at least, not word that has leaked.

Xbox announced its limited-edition Xbox Series X console variant inspired by the original Xbox back in June, in celebration of the brand's 25th anniversary.

The console and controller both sport a translucent green shell, allowing you to see all of the inner-workings of the machine and its pad. As you might expect, the console will come bundled with a matching controller, as well as the pad being able to buy separately. The console itself is expected to launch sometime this November.

Xbox does not appear to be holding a dedicated press conference at Gamescom, but will hold two days of livestreams showing off its extensive slate of upcoming titles in detail. Expect a look at games such as Gears of War: E-Day, Minecraft Dungeons 2, and Fable on Wednesday, August 26. The following day, updates for Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024, plus Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 and much more will be discussed.

As for big new surprises... perhaps we'll see some pop up in the event's main Opening Night Live showcase? As ever, IGN will be reporting on that live next Tuesday, August 25.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Subnautica 2 Early Access 1.2 Update Out Now Alongside Patch Notes, Dev Donates $100,000 to Ocean Cleanup
items.description: Subnautica 2 Early Access 1.2 is out now, adding the Buddy System to the underwater survival and crafting game. check out the patch notes in full.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Subnautica 2 Early Access 1.2 is out now, adding the Buddy System to the underwater survival and crafting game.

Developer Unknown Worlds has also announced a $100,000 donation to the appropriately named ocean cleanup non-profit The Ocean Cleanup.

Unknown Worlds previously donated a portion of proceeds from the original Subnautica to The Ocean Cleanup on World Environment Day in 2019, and has continued to support ocean conservation efforts since.

“Subnautica began with a love for the ocean, and it means a great deal to continue the conservation work we started with the original game through this donation to The Ocean Cleanup,” said executive producer Fernando Melo. “We will keep doing our part to protect the ocean we have spent so long bringing to life.”

Unknown Worlds spoke about what to expect from Subnautica 1.2 yesterday, but today's release of the update brings with it detailed patch notes, below, which include a long list of changes and fixes.

1.2 includes the first iteration of Subnautica 2 proximity chat via an in-game voice chat option that you can use with your friends to talk locally with each other. As you get farther away it will switch to a radio-sounding voice that will progressively break up to a point where you can almost not hear your friend.

Also added is player emotes via a small menu that lets players cheer on their friends, clap, or tell them you’re a little annoyed or frustrated. Inventory sharing lets players walk up to another player, access their inventory and quickly swap items between one another, rather than having to drop inventory items out in the world and have them pick them up. Player revives are also added, so if your friend is downed for whatever reason, you’ll have some time to share some oxygen with them and bring them back to life.

Two additional player characters (Grace and Jegna) are added alongside two new suit colors. Also included is the tracking tag, a short-range beacon you can throw out in the environment or put inside an inventory such as a portable locker, so if you ever leave it in a cave you can find your way back to it. If you die holding a tracking tag or have one in your inventory, it will extend your black box signal to help you find the stuff you left behind.

Improved HUD icons means all the icons will not be at full scale by default, but when you mouse over them after a half second or so they will scale up and give you the full details. Alongside that, there are improved pinned recipes, which means the UI should feel a little less confusing, and improvements to the base builder tool that should help make it clearer when you can and can't build something.

The Subnautica 2 Early Access 1.2 update patch notes, courtesy of Steam, are below:

Subnautica 2 Early Access 1.2 patch notes

Gameplay

  • 🤿Added Cross-Platform Voice Chat. Multiplayer host can choose between Global and Proximity Voice Chat (as players get further away, they become harder to hear). Voice Chat is available as “always on,” “push to talk,” or “always off.”
  • Tracking Tag added to the game. Can be placed in carryables (like a locker) as a short-range beacon. If present in hand or inventory when reprinting, will increase black box range.
  • Players can now revive each other before reprinting. Revived players will keep their equipment and regain a small amount of oxygen. Downed players can also choose to immediately reprint and respawn back at their assigned Biobed.
  • Added Wave, Clap, Thumbs Up, Thumbs Down, and Frustrated emotes. Emotes are selectable from a new radial menu. Triggerable in water or on land, and can be interrupted by gameplay input.
  • 🤿Players can now interact with each other to directly exchange inventory items.
  • Added Jegna and Grace character options in Character Customization, as well as two new color schemes for characters.
  • Interaction text on Upgrade Biobeds changed to clarify their use.
  • Added a distinct beep to player upgrade spots within a small radius.
  • Added a small flash to screen on Upgrade Biobeds.

Fauna & Flora

  • Added flinch animations and VFX to Marrowbreach, Hammerhead, Nibbler, Needlershark, Epicurean, and Twin Eel.
  • Adjusted Bulletheads so they deal more damage but can now be dodged (...sometimes).
  • Added more Coral Crab animations.
  • Revised model and animations for the Bloom Parasite.
  • Improved Jelly Ring tentacles.

Resources

  • More Carryable Racks added to early game wrecks and human-made sites.

Base Building

  • 🤿Improvements made to the base building system’s placement UI, including alignment guide lines.
  • Improvements made to how the game handles Move mode for clients in a multiplayer session.
  • Updated Tadpole Dock icon to reflect updated model.
  • Base edits now account for size snapping, such that it’s possible to fully deconstruct a room with Shrink (among other things).
  • Trashcan is now functional as a trashcan. Items added to trashcan will be destroyed one by one after a short, five second delay.
  • Bases can no longer be built inside of Great Jaw.
  • Items that are preventing an object from being built are displayed in a list.

Vehicles, Tools & Equipment

  • Changed Feedback Resonator’s interaction with creatures to stun them instead of causing them to flee.
  • Extended duration of the Sonic Resonator creature stun to 10 seconds.
  • Sources for Acid now appear as green dots in the Scanner HUD.
  • Repair Tool now unlocks after two scans.
  • Tadpoles that are destroyed outside of the Early Access fence teleport inside of the Early Access fence so that they can be recovered.

Menus & UI

  • Signals adjusted to increase clarity and reduce HUD clutter. Icons get larger as player gets closer, and text will appear on hover for signals further away.
  • Save Codes can now be directly pasted into the Cloud Save Download input box.
  • Builder menu’s scroll position persists when closing and re-opening the menu.
  • Pinned recipes highlight when the player acquires resources relevant to those recipes.
  • Items shown in Pinned Recipes are no longer dimmed, to improve readability.
  • Improved error language for errors specific to non-Game Pass Microsoft users.
  • Audiologs show elapsed and remaining playback time.

Art & Visual FX

  • VFX performance improvements to the Graveyard and its Water Slugs, for the players who collect hundreds of Water Slugs.
  • Tallshrooms now have an icon in the Scanner HUD.
  • Added impact VFX for Tongue Thief.
  • Light poles connecting Observatory and Rosetta Stone added.
  • Removed odd blue outline that was sometimes visible on Collector Leviathan.
  • Improved consistency of sparks VFX across the game.
  • Improved consistency of electricity VFX across the game.
  • Added shock VFX for Hammerheads impacting objects.
  • Added more environmental effects to abandoned outposts and wrecks.

Voice & Narrative

  • Previously unlocalized lines are now localized.
  • Naming of Carryable Racks is now consistent across the game, instead of sometimes being “Wall Rack” or “Hardpoint.”
  • Reduced frequency of NOA alerts.
  • Adjusted Welcome Center message in Spanish and Italian.
  • Adjusted pacing of dialog to better match the actions occurring during the recordings.
  • Added Databank entry for Mod Station.
  • Added Databank entries for audiologs that were missing them.
  • Further refinements to voice over prioritization, so the most important lines are heard.

Music & SFX

  • Music added to Tufa Zona, Thermal Area, and North Coral Gardens.

Miscellaneous

  • New Privacy Policy additions from July 15th will pop up on first play.
  • New Frame Generation modes 5x and 6x (RTX 5000 series) added.
  • New Dynamic Frame Generation added. Will automatically select the appropriate Frame Generation mode to get a good performance (RTX 5000 series).
  • VSync and DLSS Frame Generation can be turned on at the same time.
  • Added description for Nvidia Reflex in Settings.
  • Reorganized order of volume sliders.
  • The in-game Feedback Tool now allows attaching a save file.

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed Collector Leviathan performing a 360 spin whenever it grabs or throws a Tadpole.
  • Fixed an issue where settings menus would sometimes become cut-off while navigating with controller/gamepad.
  • 🤿Fixed an exploit where swapping the resource in an occupied Metal Farm caused the new resource to inherit the growth time of the previous resource.
  • 🤿Fixed an issue where opened Angel Combs’ cankers could incorrectly appear closed after a game update.
  • Pausing the game while sprinting no longer causes the player to permanently sprint.
  • Fixed some Axum/Tailings furniture being buildable outside of the player’s base, which caused multiple knock-on problems.
  • Tadpole can no longer be docked when there is insufficient space for it, resolving an issue where the Tadpole could become stuck in its dock.
  • 🤿Additional fixes to the tool prompts to account for accuracy and recipe-sharing between players in a multiplayer session.
  • Fixed Power Transmitter ray visibility and overall appearance, particularly for multiplayer clients who alternately saw extra rays or had rays that should be there disappear.
  • 🤿Fixed Hydroturbines stopping their power production after 120-160 mins of gameplay, after the player swam away from them, and for their turbines to stop spinning, even when producing power.
  • Fixed music playing in the incorrect region or not playing at all in intended areas.
  • Fixed a soft lock where using Unstuck during the Lifepod launch cutscene would cause the player to teleport back to the Deep Start awakening room after the cutscene.
  • Fixed an issue where pressing the spacebar during the TOS skipped the step of agreeing to it.
  • Fixed an issue where the Collector Leviathan would release a captured player if the Camouflage Biomod activated during the eating scene.
  • Fixed an issue where chassis signals could remain visible on screen even when the chassis is equipped to the Tadpole.
  • Fixed the player’s dive mask clipping into the camera while adjusting FOV in the Settings menu.
  • 🤿Fixed several terrain, resource, and world object clipping, floating, gap, extended collision, misplacement, and texture issues.
  • 🤿Fixed an issue where the battery terminal in the Welcome Center could be accessed through the exterior wall.
  • Fixed Jetocaris’s PDA image not matching the in-game creature model.
  • Fixed Feedback Resonator VO playing on unlocking the recipe and after crafting it, instead of just when it’s crafted.
  • Fixed Cicada Wreck (Stairway to Heaven) databank entry not unlocking when entering the relevant area.
  • Fixed Metal Farm voice over playing when reaching the Axum Metal Farms in the Root Canyon, instead of when the Metal Farm is scanned.
  • Fixed an issue where Algae Blocks and Nutrient Blocks couldn’t be used as BioReactor fuel.
  • Correction to Question 6 in the Tadpole Pens dialog with a certain terminal.
  • Necrolei Cysts can now be planted in Growbeds.
  • Fixed an issue where using Unstuck while holding a carryable Utility would prevent players from being able to pick up other Utilities or equip hotbar items.
  • Added corrections to the scannable highlight for objects that were missing it.
  • Fixed Sophie’s Riot In Progress audiolog playing when picked up.
  • Fixed some external base decorations that should have had movement appearing inactive after saving and loading the game.
  • Fixed Time of Day Display showing the wrong icon during its scanning process.
  • Fixed some Quartz Memory Chips using different titles in the Databank entries, as compared to their HUD text.
  • Fixed missing SFX during Chap Blackbox audio playback.
  • Fixed an issue where the player’s camera could get stuck in place after trying to undock a blocked Tadpole three times.
  • Fixed certain investigations appearing in the Databank under “Closed Investigations” when they were still active.
  • Fixed Sandspear getting stunned while underground.
  • Fixed “You are being hunted” voice over failing to play when the player encounters a Marrowbreach for the first time at Camp One.
  • Fixed Hammerheads sinking to the seafloor too quickly after being stunned.

  • Added several fixes for scannable objects being unscannable in specific locations.

  • Fixed the “Close” button keybind on Pioneer Selection being nonfunctional.

  • Fixed an issue where the Tadpole’s collision could become offset from its model, for the host of a multiplayer session, if a client in that session exited the Tadpole while it was moving.
  • Fixed an issue where Sandspears would float out of the ground, while acting like they were in the ground, if their nest location was blocked by an object like a base or Tadpole.
  • Sealed off an area where the player could get under the map near the east side of Power Plant.

  • 🤿Fixed an issue where the “Warning Power Offline” message would play when Metal Farms finished production, despite the Farms still being powered.
  • 🤿Fixed an issue where Metal Farms connected in a series would lose power when the starting Metal Farm, connected to base power, completed resource production.
  • 🤿Fixed an issue where plantables would remain floating and functional after refunding a base that included a Growbed.

  • Fixed an issue where bringing up the Steam Overlay didn’t pause the game.

Subnautica 2 Early Access 1.2 is out now, adding the Buddy System to the underwater survival and crafting game.

Developer Unknown Worlds has also announced a $100,000 donation to the appropriately named ocean cleanup non-profit The Ocean Cleanup.

Unknown Worlds previously donated a portion of proceeds from the original Subnautica to The Ocean Cleanup on World Environment Day in 2019, and has continued to support ocean conservation efforts since.

“Subnautica began with a love for the ocean, and it means a great deal to continue the conservation work we started with the original game through this donation to The Ocean Cleanup,” said executive producer Fernando Melo. “We will keep doing our part to protect the ocean we have spent so long bringing to life.”

Unknown Worlds spoke about what to expect from Subnautica 1.2 yesterday, but today's release of the update brings with it detailed patch notes, below, which include a long list of changes and fixes.

1.2 includes the first iteration of Subnautica 2 proximity chat via an in-game voice chat option that you can use with your friends to talk locally with each other. As you get farther away it will switch to a radio-sounding voice that will progressively break up to a point where you can almost not hear your friend.

Also added is player emotes via a small menu that lets players cheer on their friends, clap, or tell them you’re a little annoyed or frustrated. Inventory sharing lets players walk up to another player, access their inventory and quickly swap items between one another, rather than having to drop inventory items out in the world and have them pick them up. Player revives are also added, so if your friend is downed for whatever reason, you’ll have some time to share some oxygen with them and bring them back to life.

Two additional player characters (Grace and Jegna) are added alongside two new suit colors. Also included is the tracking tag, a short-range beacon you can throw out in the environment or put inside an inventory such as a portable locker, so if you ever leave it in a cave you can find your way back to it. If you die holding a tracking tag or have one in your inventory, it will extend your black box signal to help you find the stuff you left behind.

Improved HUD icons means all the icons will not be at full scale by default, but when you mouse over them after a half second or so they will scale up and give you the full details. Alongside that, there are improved pinned recipes, which means the UI should feel a little less confusing, and improvements to the base builder tool that should help make it clearer when you can and can't build something.

The Subnautica 2 Early Access 1.2 update patch notes, courtesy of Steam, are below:

Gameplay

  • 🤿Added Cross-Platform Voice Chat. Multiplayer host can choose between Global and Proximity Voice Chat (as players get further away, they become harder to hear). Voice Chat is available as “always on,” “push to talk,” or “always off.”
  • Tracking Tag added to the game. Can be placed in carryables (like a locker) as a short-range beacon. If present in hand or inventory when reprinting, will increase black box range.
  • Players can now revive each other before reprinting. Revived players will keep their equipment and regain a small amount of oxygen. Downed players can also choose to immediately reprint and respawn back at their assigned Biobed.
  • Added Wave, Clap, Thumbs Up, Thumbs Down, and Frustrated emotes. Emotes are selectable from a new radial menu. Triggerable in water or on land, and can be interrupted by gameplay input.
  • 🤿Players can now interact with each other to directly exchange inventory items.

  • Adjusted Bulletheads so they deal more damage but can now be dodged (...sometimes).

items.title: Demon Hunter Sues Netflix Over KPop Demon Hunters, as Christian Metal Band Claims Fans Bought Tickets for Wrong Show
items.description: Christian metal band Demon Hunter is suing KPop Demon Hunters streamer Netflix.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Christian metal band Demon Hunter is suing KPop Demon Hunters streamer Netflix.

In a trademark lawsuit, the Seattle-based musicians alleged that the similarity between their group name and that of the globally-renowned animated movie had caused "substantial confusion," particularly as Netflix mounts plans for a worldwide KPop concert tour.

According to legal documentation seen by BBC News, Demon Hunter (the band) claim that their "carefully built" musical identity established over more than 25 years now faces an "existential crisis" due to the recent surge in popularity for the Huntr/X trio.

To illustrate their claim, Demon Hunter's litigation points to an incident where a KPop Demon Hunters fan allegedly spent $500 on tickets to one of their shows, only to discover it was a metal concert and not the family-friendly animated extravaganza they were expecting.

Other examples of a few people getting the two entities confused reportedly include incidents where Demon Hunter has been erroneously tagged on social media in KPop-related discussions, and when a TV producer contacted the group thinking they were something to do with Netflix.

Formed in 2000, Demon Hunter have released 13 albums to date, featuring songs such as "My Throat Is an Open Grave," "Dead Flowers," and "Snap Your Fingers, Snap Your Neck." Popular songs from Kpop Demon Hunters include "Golden," "Takedown," and "Soda Pop."

Released in 2025, KPop Demon Hunters is now the most-watched original title in Netflix history, beating even Squid Game, Wednesday, and Stranger Things. It is also now the winner of both Best Animated Feature and Best Original Song at the most recent Golden Globes and Academy Awards. A sequel is also in the works, though will likely not arrive before 2029.

Demon Hunters have asked the court to stop Netflix using the KPop Demon Hunters name for recorded music, live shows and merchandise, and to award unspecified damages.

Image credit: Stephen J. Cohen/Getty, Netflix.

items.title: RuneScape: Dragonwilds Confirmed for Day One Xbox Game Pass Launch
items.description: RuneScape: Dragonwilds will be available as a day one Xbox Game Pass title next month, developer Jagex has announced.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
RuneScape: Dragonwilds will be available as a day one Xbox Game Pass title next month, developer Jagex has announced.

The open world, co-op, crafting and survival game is the first standalone title in Jagex’s long-running medieval MMORPG franchise, and the first RuneScape game set for consoles. It’s sold over 1 million copies during early access already.

Here’s the official blurb:

Players embark solo or in teams of four across Gielinor’s previously unexplored continent of Ashenfall, on an epic quest to discover why untamed, transformative magic spills across the fractured land.
Through the power of magic that flows through the anima-rich landscape, players can not only obtain powerful spells to get them through battles, but find their practical uses as well, as they collect items and craft things to help them throughout their journey. In this land riddled with fierce dragons, players must level up skills, prepare potions, and craft gear, as they carve a path through these ferocious beasts and make their way to the Dragon Queen herself.

RuneScape: Dragonwilds launches on September 15 in 1.0 form, which includes the brand-new Scorned Wilderness update, alongside all content from the upcoming Umbral Sands expansion. As confirmed at State of Play in June, RuneScape: Dragonwilds is also a day one launch on PlayStation Plus Extra and Premium.

RuneScape: Dragonwilds launches its 1.0 version in both Digital Standard and Deluxe Editions for PC via Steam, the Jagex Launcher, and Epic Games Store on September 15, alongside its release on PlayStation 5 (and on PlayStation Plus Extra and Premium tiers for subscribers), and Xbox Series X and S.

The game will also be available as a Digital Standard Edition on Nintendo Switch 2 on September 15. Physical Standard and Deluxe Editions of RuneScape: Dragonwilds will be available for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X in Q4 2026.

Microsoft has yet to announce September Game Pass games beyond Shelldiver (Cloud, Console, and PC), which hits Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass on September 1. Here's everything coming to Xbox Game Pass during the rest of August.

items.title: New LEGO Batman DLC Trailer to Debut on IGN’s gamescom Livestream
items.description: Get a sneak peek at LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight’s Mayhem Collection DLC with an exclusive trailer and developer interview during IGN’s gamescom livestream.
items.author: Michael Peyton
items.content:
LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight’s upcoming DLC won’t be out for another month, but you can get a sneak preview very soon. A brand-new trailer for the game’s Mayhem Collection DLC will be shown exclusively during IGN’s gamescom Studio programming Wednesday, August 26.

The game, from TT Games and Warner Bros. Games, released this past May. According to our review, it features “a strong open-world Gotham and trademark Lego slapstick humour [powering] a fantastic plastic parody of Batman’s greatest hits." The Mayhem Collection DLC comes out September 18 and is included for players who purchased the LEGO Batman's Deluxe Edition.

According to LEGO, the Mayhem Collection features “the Joker and Harley Quinn as playable characters, each with their own abilities and gadgets, along with a new story mission, new Mayhem Mode, new outfits for the original playable characters, new Batcave items, and a new Batmobile."

In addition to a new trailer, IGN’s gamescom programming will feature a deep-dive interview with LEGO Batman’s Lead Designer Tim Spence and and Advanced Designer Chris Payne, who will be on hand to break down what players can expect when the DLC launches in a few weeks.

Fans can catch both the trailer and the interview close to the beginning of IGN’s gamescom Studio Wednesday broadcast at 6am PT / 9am ET / 3pm CEST on August 26.

IGN’s gamescom programming runs throughout the week and also features exclusive looks at major games including Fable, Control Resonant, Dune: Awakening, Crimson Desert, Persona 4 Revival, Alien: Isolation 2, Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and many more.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is available now for Windows, PS5, and XBOX Series X/S. The game launches September 18 on Nintendo Switch 2.

items.title: Redfall Director Pleaded With Microsoft to Release Final Patch, Despite Already Being 'Fired'
items.description: Legendary game designer Harvey Smith has said he pleaded with Microsoft to let his team release one final patch to improve the poorly-received Xbox console exclusive Redfall — even though he had been "fired."
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Legendary game designer Harvey Smith has said he pleaded with Microsoft to let his team release one final patch to improve the poorly-received Xbox console exclusive Redfall — even though he had been "fired."

First-person vampire shooter Redfall launched to negative reviews in 2023, and proved to be the final project for Arkane Austin, the Texas-based team behind 2017's Prey, which also worked on Dishonored and its sequel.

Smith, who served as lead game designer on 2000's Deus Ex, then creative director of Dishonored and Dishonored 2, found himself out of work in May 2024 when it was announced that Arkane Austin would be shut down, with ongoing work on Redfall's post-launch roadmap canned as a result.

But the studio had been hard at work on another patch for the game, version 1.4, which would address numerous player issues and bugbears. Speaking to The Game Business, Smith revealed for the first time that he had to negotiate with Microsoft to be let back into the office to ensure this patch saw the light of day.

"We finished the game and it was very poorly received," Smith recalled. "We then worked on it for a year. We patched thousands of bugs. We then got laid off, but we had in the pipe version 1.4. It was the one that fixed tons of stuff. So, we went to Microsoft and said, ‘I know we don't work here anymore, but can we please release this?' And to their credit, they did not say no.

"They let six or seven of us sign forms that we could come back in the building. After being fired, we released 1.4, which I think if we had that on day one, it wouldn't have set the world on fire, but it was a much, much better game."

Redfall was a distinct departure from the immersive sims that Arkane was known for, cooked up during the heady days of the games industry's push for live-service elements. (It's a push that we're still seeing the effects of now, as Sony reportedly reboots its Horizon multiplayer game following negative feedback.)

"That was a difficult project," Smith concluded, discussing Redfall in general. "Arkane is very specialized, but the industry is growing, and there’s always more mouths to feed. And it's great when you can reach a wider audience. We got swept up in the games-as-a-service thing, and I had the foolish chutzpah to assume that it always works out for us. We can do this. Let's take what we love, and mix it with [games-as-a-service]. And do different mechanics by day and night. And have character classes. Then in the middle of all that, COVID happened."

Two years on, the fate of another Arkane development studio now also hangs in the balance. Arkane Lyon, which is currently building Marvel's Blade, is now in the process of being sold as part of the Xbox "reset" — though exactly what will happen to the team and it's project still remains to be seen.

As for Smith himself, IGN has just reported on the reveal of his new game development studio, Black Pony Immersive. The fledgling team, backed by other former Arkane talent, will once again focus on the immersive sim genre that Smith helped pioneer.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Dishonored, Deus Ex Designer Stars New Studio to Continue Focusing on Immersive Sims
items.description: Decorated veteran game developer Harvey Smith (Dishonored series, original Deus Ex series), most recently of Arkane Austin – which Xbox shut down in 2024 following the failure of Redfall – has opened a new game development studio. Dubbed Black Pony Immersive, it will indeed focus on the "immersive sim" genre that Smith helped pioneer evolve through his work as co-creative director on Dishonored, creative director on Dishonored 2, and lead game designer on the original Deus Ex, and the team includes a number of former Arkane Austin developers.
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
Decorated veteran game developer Harvey Smith (Dishonored series, original Deus Ex series), most recently of Arkane Austin – which Xbox shut down in 2024 following the failure of Redfall – has opened a new game development studio. Dubbed Black Pony Immersive, it will indeed focus on the "immersive sim" genre that Smith helped pioneer evolve through his work as co-creative director on Dishonored, creative director on Dishonored 2, and lead game designer on the original Deus Ex (which, not for nothing, this particular writer ranks as a top-10 game of all-time).

"My favorite gaming memories come from seeing players approach challenges with creativity, deep-diving into our world building," Smith said. "We try to reward players for their curiosity and exploration. At our new studio, we're building exactly the kind of single-player games we're most passionate about."

Smith is a disciple of immersive-sim legend Warren Spector, who just announced his retirement. "I worked closely with Warren for nine years, learning a lot," Smith told IGN. "We still go to lunch now and then. Recently, he gave me one of his guitars after we ate a bunch of Mexican food. My feelings for Warren are deep and complicated, but mostly I feel admiration and gratitude. For Richard Garriott too. So much good came of Origin. Places like Austin or Boston, or cities in Europe, experience flourishes now and then, as creative leaders get something going. A scene. The entire industry is deeply hurting right now, Austin included. I am just thrilled to be announcing Black Pony Immersive. Making another run at trying to create magic for players. Having the team we have, including Ricardo and people we worked with on Deus Ex, Dishonored, and Prey just feels like a dream. We are on fire for single-player, narrative-driven, first-person (highly hyphenated) immersive sims."

"We are on fire for single-player, narrative-driven, first-person (highly hyphenated) immersive sims."

I asked about lessons learned from Arkane to hopefully help lead Black Pony to a better fate, and Smith said, "In my mind, that's a tricky, emotional question. I loved my time there with Raf, Ricardo, Ben, and everyone else. I worked at Arkane for 16 years. Part of the company is still around, in Lyon, where it started. During my years there, we went back and forth between Texas and France. The company released Dishonored, Prey, Dishonored 2, some great Dishonored DLC, Death of the Outsider, Mooncrash, and Deathloop. We worked on a few other projects too, including Redfall at the end. You say, 'a better fate.' But honestly imagine if, like Arkane, our new studio lasted 27+ years, and released at least 4-5 absolute bangers, on top of being a super fun, interesting place to work, a place that experienced what I can only describe as electric fan support. If that happens again, I will absolutely count myself as blessed. I would feel lucky in the extreme to experience that again. And I don't know of many places that get to that much joy and creative success. It's just so rare. Very hard to pull off."

I concluded by asking Smith if he felt a sense of responsibility to carry the torch for the immersive sim genre. "Always. Until I am dead," he said. items.title: Horizon 3 Only Has a 'Tiny Team' Working on It at Guerrilla, Reportedly Still Years Away
items.description: Horizon 3 remains years away from release, with a “tiny team” said to be working on planning it out at developer Guerrilla Games.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Horizon 3 remains years away from release, with a “tiny team” said to be working on planning it out at developer Guerrilla Games.

A new report into the fate of multiplayer spinoff Horizon Hunters Gathering from Bloomberg also contains a brief update on the next single-player Horizon game, which is set to continue Aloy’s story from 2017’s Zero Dawn and 2022’s Forbidden West.

"A tiny team has been plotting out the next single-player Horizon game but it remains years away from completion, according to the people familiar with the studio’s plans,” Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier reported.

Rather than jump straight into Horizon 3 after Forbidden West, Guerrilla Games focused on Horizon Hunters Gathering, which is now being rebooted. The wait for Horizon 3, then, could be many years away. If true, perhaps it’s targeting the PlayStation 6. If that’s true, it would mean the Horizon series skips the PlayStation 5 generation in terms of mainline games designed exclusively for the console (Forbidden West was a cross-gen game that launched on PS4 and PS5).

A full-blown sequel to Horizon: Forbidden West was confirmed to be in the works when Guerrilla mentioned "Aloy's next adventure" in April 2023. In October last year, Sony was said to be targeting 2026 for filming of its live-action Horizon Zero Dawn movie, with a release at some point in 2027.

There also appears to be a third game in development at Guerrilla. Bloomberg said some staff who were working on Horizon Hunters Gathering have now been moved to a mystery project that is set for evaluation at the end of this year.

Horizon Hunters Gathering isn't the only multiplayer game set in the Horizon universe. Bizarrely, NCSoft and Sony are working on Horizon Steel Frontiers, a massively multiplayer online role-playing game designed for mobile devices, but also playable on PC. NCSoft is said to be working closely with Guerrilla to craft the world, but this is very much an NCSoft-developed game.

items.title: PlayStation Reportedly Reboots Horizon Multiplayer Spinoff Following Negative Feedback
items.description: Sony has reportedly rebooted PlayStation live-service game Horizon Hunters Gathering after negative feedback from playtests.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Sony has reportedly rebooted PlayStation live-service game Horizon Hunters Gathering after negative feedback from playtests.

Horizon Hunters Gathering is a multiplayer, cartoony spinoff from Guerrilla’s mainline, single-player Horizon series, which is known for its photorealistic visuals. Upon its announcement in February, Horizon Hunters Gathering was compared to Capcom’s Monster Hunter series, although many questioned whether it would find an audience.

Closed playtests followed earlier this year, with a launch across PlayStation 5 and PC expected to follow. However, according to Bloomberg, Sony has ordered a reboot of the game amid negative feedback from the playtests. Apparently, Guerrilla has been working to reboot the game since June, and plans to strip out the live-service parts of the game to make it “a traditional cooperative multiplayer game with a story mode and a far smaller scope.”

It sounds like there is a great deal of pressure on this reboot, too. Bloomberg said staff were told this week that Guerrilla has until December to impress PlayStation bosses with the game’s next milestone. It’s not canceled, but it sounds like it could be. Some Horizon Hunters Gathering staff are being moved over to another Guerrilla project with a milestone due at the end of this year, Bloomberg added.

Apparently a “tiny team” is working on the next Horizon single-player game, which we’ll call Horizon 3 but will undoubtedly carry a new subtitle, but it’s still years away.

When Horizon Hunters Gathering was announced, game director Arjan Bak said that in the game you'd fight deadly machines in tactical three-player co-op action and adapt your Hunter for intense missions.

"Combat is tactical, reactive, and deeply skill-based, building on the tactical precision of the Horizon games while embracing the dynamics of team play," Bak said at the time. "The foundation of Horizon Hunters Gathering centers around challenging and replayable hunts."

Bak confirmed two game modes: Machine Incursion, which was described as "a high-intensity mission" where waves of machines pour out from underground gateways, led by a "formidable boss"; and Cauldron Descent, a longer, multi-stage trial in which "ever-changing rooms push Hunters to their limits, from brutal machine encounters to hidden doors that promise power and reward for teams prepared to open them." Both modes were available in the closed playtests.

There's a roster of Hunters to play as, each with distinct melee or ranged playstyles and weapons. Bak said there was also a roguelite perk system to craft the build you want. Story wise, there was a narrative campaign "which will introduce new mysteries, characters, and threats, but we’re keeping it under wraps for now," Bak said back in February. "What we can say is that Hunters Gathering is fully canon and its story doesn’t stop at launch!"

The social hub is the name of the game: Hunters Gathering. It was "a vibrant social hub where players can connect, prepare, and celebrate victories together. Here, you can customize your Hunters, visit vendors, upgrade gear, and team up for your next adventure."

It is unclear how much of this, if any, remains in the rebooted version of the game.

Horizon Hunters Gathering is yet more trouble for Sony’s embattled live service ambition, which now appears to be in full retreat. While Arrowhead’s Helldivers 2 was a breakout hit, becoming the fastest-selling PlayStation Studios game of all time with 12 million copies sold in just 12 weeks, Sony’s other live service games were either canceled or suffered disastrous launches.

Indeed, Sony’s Concord is one of the biggest video game disasters in PlayStation history, lasting just a couple of weeks before it was brought offline amid eye-wateringly low player numbers. Sony later decided to kill the game entirely and shut its developer.

The Concord flop came after Sony had already canceled Naughty Dog’s The Last of Us multiplayer game. Last year, Sony reportedly canceled two unannounced live service games, one a God of War title in development at Bluepoint, the other in the works at Days Gone developer Bend.

Sony announced plans in February 2022 to launch more than 10 live service games by March 2026, later saying the push would bring games of different genres to different audiences. It spent big on studio buyouts as part of the drive, bringing in Destiny and Marathon developer Bungie, Jade Raymond's Haven Studios, and the now shuttered Firewalk Studios.

But in 2023, Sony president Hiroki Totoki said the company was reviewing the 12 live service PlayStation games it had in the works, and committed to launching only six of them by the end of financial year 2025, meaning by the end of March 2026. At the time, Totoki said Sony was still working on when the other six live service games would come out, adding: "It's not that we stick to certain titles, but for the gamers quality should be the most important.”

In April, the director of The Last of Us multiplayer spinoff spoke out on the “devastating” impact of its cancellation, which he only found out about 24 hours before Sony made it public. Vinit Agarwal also explained Sony's ill-fated push into live service.

“What happened was, during COVID, the game industry saw a huge growth because everyone was at home,” Agarwal said. “So in 2020, money was flooding into the game industry because people were playing a lot more games all of a sudden because they're at home. What else did they have to do?

“Not just that, online games specifically saw a huge boost because people wanted to play with their friends. They couldn't see their friends, so they had to play online with their friends. So online games got a huge boon. So Sony decided to put a lot of money into online gaming like everyone else was. And so that was part of why The Last of Us Multiplayer got funding, and we got off the ground and we made a lot of progress, and the game was doing really, really well internally. We developed it almost to 80% completion. It was very very close to done.

“But then all the forces that pushed the game industry in 2020 were the reasons it started declining in 2022, 2023. So as people returned to the office, suddenly people didn't have as much time to play games. You know, that spending reduced. The economy also went down. And so all that money that flooded into the game industry was not going to be able to sustain. Because money was getting pulled out, they had to also kind of collapse the spending they'd spent. They overspent basically. They were overzealous.”

Horizon Hunters Gathering isn't the only multiplayer game set in the Horizon universe. Bizarrely, NCSoft and Sony are working on Horizon Steel Frontiers, a massively multiplayer online role-playing game designed for mobile devices, but also playable on PC. NCSoft is said to be working closely with Guerrilla to craft the world, but this is very much an NCSoft-developed game.

items.title: Subnautica 2 Patch Adds Buddy System, Dev Reveals Glimpse at Early Access 2 Update
items.description: Subnautica 2 gets its Buddy system update today, August 19. It adds a number of new features revolving around multiplayer in the underwater survival and crafting game. Here's what to expect from the 1.2 update.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Subnautica 2 gets its Buddy system update today, August 19. It adds a number of new features revolving around multiplayer in the underwater survival and crafting game.

In a new video, creative director Anthony Gallegos ran through everything players can expect from the co-op focused 1.2 update, which adds Proximity Chat, Player Trading and Revives, and an all-new Tracking Tag.

Gallegos said 1.2 includes developer Unknown Worlds’ first iteration of Subnautica 2 proximity chat. It includes an in-game voice chat option that you can use with your friends to talk locally with each other. As you get farther away it will switch to a radio-sounding voice that will progressively break up to a point where you can almost not hear your friend. “I think it definitely adds to the tension of it,” Gallegos said.

Also added is player emotes via a small menu that lets players cheer on their friends, clap, or tell them you’re a little annoyed or frustrated. Gallegos said he’s looking forward to seeing players use these emotes out of context to create fun moments, such as sarcastically clapping.

Inventory sharing lets players walk up behind another player, access their inventory and quickly swap items between one another, rather than having to drop inventory items out in the world and have them pick them up.

Player revives are also added, so if your friend is downed for whatever reason, you’ll have some time to share some oxygen with them and bring them back to life.

Two additional player characters (Grace and Jegna) are added alongside two new suit colors, “which should help with a little bit more of the diversification of players when you’re in multiplayer,” Gallegos explained. “You can still all look like the same character if you want — that’s something we support — but we like to have more options for you, and we will continue to roll out new options as we go through early access.”

Also included is the tracking tag, a short-range beacon you can throw out in the environment or put inside an inventory such as a portable locker, so if you ever leave it in a cave you can find your way back to it. If you die holding a tracking tag or have one in your inventory, it will extend your black box signal to help you find the stuff you left behind.

Improved HUD icons means all the icons will not be at full scale by default, but when you mouse over them after a half second or so they will scale up and give you the full details. “This is really nice because when you get really farther away from a region and you might have like six beacons, you turn and look at it, they're all really grouped together. But this allows you to more precisely pick the one that you want to know the information for without it feeling so busy on the HUD,” Gallegos said.

Alongside that, there are improved pinned recipes, which means the UI should feel a little less confusing, and improvements to the base builder tool that should help make it clearer when you can and can't build something.

Gallegos said this is just a chunk of the larger features added in 1.2, so expect more when the patch notes are available. Meanwhile, Unknown Worlds is continuing to work on the Early Access 2 update, which adds the new region, new story, new progression, new vehicles, and a lot more. The video showed a tantalizing glimpse at gameplay footage of this work-in-progress.

“The whole reason that we do make games at Unknown Worlds in this way is because we think we make the best games possible when you participate in this development alongside us,” Gallegos concluded. “And I think that this update shows that we really want to listen and prioritize the things that our fans are asking for.”

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: GTA 6 Leak Forces Stop Killing Games Movement to Distance Itself From Hacker Manifesto
items.description: The Stop Killing Games movement has distanced itself from the manifesto published by the alleged group behind last night’s GTA 6 leak, and cast doubt on their motivations.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
The Stop Killing Games movement has distanced itself from the manifesto published by the alleged group behind last night’s GTA 6 leak, and cast doubt on their motivations.

Yesterday, two videos showing apparent GTA 6 gameplay, and an image reportedly of the complete map, hit the internet. The assets contain a watermark that advertises a cryptocurrency and a website that reportedly belong to a group called 'CyberLeek.' The website contains three demands of Rockstar Games and other video game publishers, seemingly in response to the all-digital future that has seen such backlash online in recent months.

Rockstar, specifically, has come under fire for failing to sell GTA 6 on a physical disc, forcing fans to download it or buy a box without a code inside instead. Rockstar also locks some content behind the more expensive $100 Ultimate Edition of GTA 6, which has also sparked some criticism. Meanwhile, GTA 6 preorders went live before gameplay was officially shown.

Contained within the CyberLeek manifesto is criticism of 2014 racing game The Crew, which was at the heart of the Stop Killing Games consumer movement. CyberLeek also threatened other video game publishers, presumably with gameplay leaks such as this one suffered by GTA 6. “Publishers should beware,” the manifesto concludes. “If CyberLeek can reach Rockstar, no one is safe. This is a message to all big corpo: behave, or be the next target.”

The Stop Killing Games movement was launched by YouTuber Ross Scott in April 2024 after Ubisoft shut down the servers for The Crew, rendering it completely unplayable. items.title: Don't Skip Your Chance to Compete in The UNO Championship Series, With a $50,000 Grand Finale Prize
items.description: How good are you at UNO? Toy company Mattel is announcing the UNO World Championship Series, which will offer a $50,000 grand prize.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
How good are you at UNO? This year, toy company Mattel is announcing the UNO World Championship Series, which will take the fast-paced card game to the world stage with a $50,000 grand prize.

Fancy your chances? Taking a shot at the tournament is as easy as joining in via the UNO! Mobile app, or turning up to in-person qualifiers to be held across the country in Orlando (October 3), Chicago (October 10) and Los Angeles (October 17).

Successful contestants will then compete on the world stage in the UNO World Championship grand final, broadcast live from L.A. on November 11, and available to watch globally via Twitch.

If the honor of being crowed the first UNO World Champion isn't enough of a draw (pun intended), then the $50,000 prize money will likely sweeten the deal (sorry).

"At its core, UNO has always been about creating unforgettable moments around the table from epic comebacks to game-changing Draw 4s," Katie Buford, VP and Global Head of Mattel Games said. "The 2026 UNO Championship Series Tournament brings that excitement to the biggest stage yet, giving fans around the world a front-row seat as elite players battle it out to become this year's UNO champion."

Can't make it to L.A.? No worries. If you want to up your UNO game to the championship level then Mattel is launching a range of prize-worthy products for you to play with at home. These include the UNO Championship Series Tournament Set ($19.99) which includes a snazzy UNO set, scoring pad and gold trophy.

A separate UNO Championship Series Belt ($19.99) will also be available, as will a Championship Series Card Shuffler ($19.99). For the pros, the UNO Championship Series Expanded Tournament Set ($27.99) is the ultimate offering, with a more robust gold trophy for the champ.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: The Pokémon Company Cancels 30th Anniversary Card Orders Following 'Cyber Incident,' Warns of Customer Data Breach
items.description: The Pokémon Company is cancelling orders of Pokémon 30th Anniversary Cards following a "cyber incident" that potentially left customer details exposed.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
The Pokémon Company is cancelling orders of Pokémon 30th Anniversary Cards following a "cyber incident" that potentially left customer details exposed.

That's according to emails shared online by fans impacted by the incident, who previously pre-ordered Pokémon trading cards purchased via the Pokémon Center website.

The breach appears to be isolated to European orders, which the Pokémon Company planned to fulfil using local logistics firm CEVA. If that name sounds familiar, it's because this is the same firm that Valve recently warned customers had been hit by data theft, similarly impacting those who had recently bought Steam hardware.

🚨 POKEMON CENTER CYBER ATTACK, CANCELLED ORDERS ARE STOLEN PERSONAL INFO 🚨

Looks like 30th celebration orders have been cancelled for some people and their personal information has been stolen 😭 pic.twitter.com/C8hH6xBOFO

— Parvy (@Parvytcg) August 14, 2026

Exactly how many Pokémon customers have also been impacted is unclear. It has also not been explained why purchases are being fully cancelled, something that was not the case for those who bought Steam Decks and Steam Machines. IGN has contacted the Pokémon Company for comment.

"We are writing to let you know about a cyber incident affecting a Pokémon Center logistics provider that may affect some of your information," the Pokémon Company's email warns. "To fulfil your Pokémon Center orders, CEVA receives delivery-related information to ship your Pokémon Center products.

"We understand that the following information regarding your Pokémon Center purchases may have been obtained by unauthorized parties from CEVA: Your full name, your mailing address (street address, post code, city, country), your phone number, your email address, details of the contents of your PokemonCenter.com order(s)."

The news will certainly not help ongoing issues with Pokémon card scarcity, which has prompted U.S. retailer Target to begin slicing open boxes to deter scalpers. In Japan, some releases are being limited to Japanese residents only, while facial recognition for adults and children has been rolled out in some locations to limit daily card purchases.

Pokémon cards have become a prime target for scalpers and thieves over the past few years due to their soaring popularity and the perceived value of rare cards. New card releases frequently sell out completely, and The Pokémon Company has appeared unable or unwilling to fully keep up with demand — despite a staggering 10 billion cards printed last year alone.

Looking to start your collection? We've also got a list of the 10 most expensive Pokémon cards of 2026 so far.

items.title: Deleted Highlander Action Sequence With The Kurgan Was Cut Because It Was 'Too Good,' Actor Says
items.description: An actor who starred in a fight sequence cut from the original Highlander movie has revealed what happened, 40 years later.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
An actor who starred in a fight sequence cut from the original Highlander movie has revealed what happened, 40 years later.

Swordsman Alex King told The Telegraph that he filmed a sword fight with Clancy Brown, who played the towering villain The Kurgan, in 1985 in London. But the sequence was cut from the film — something King, who was in his late twenties at the time, had no knowledge of. His name did not appear in the credits, nor was he invited to attend screenings.

King played an immortal called Yung Dol Kim, who is beheaded in traditional Highlander fashion by The Kurgan after what was described as an “ambitious” fight sequence. Yung Dol Kim, at peace with his fate, kneels for the final blow, smiling as The Kurgan’s sword comes down.

According to The Telegraph, the film’s fight choreographer, swordmaster Bob Anderson (who appeared as a stunt double for Darth Vader's lightsaber battles in The Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi) warned that the choreography risked overshadowing even the action scenes starring Christopher Lambert’s protagonist, Connor MacLeod. King, now 69, was a regional level-4 fencing instructor at the time he shot the scene.

Highlander fans will get a kick out of this description of the deleted scene, per The Telegraph:

At the studio, King and Anderson built a fight unlike anything else in the film. They had him wield two swords against Brown’s single blade, with kicks and acrobatic dives. One move sent him hurtling backwards over a bank of computers, only to dive back into frame, grab both hilts and fight on. The sequence’s most radical element was its ending. Yung Dol Kim doesn’t lose; he simply stops. After centuries, he has had enough and chooses to die, kneeling before the Kurgan. “I wanted to go from an expression of violent combat to the serene face of a man who has, Buddha-like, embraced his death.”

“I think they were embarrassed,” King said of the decision to cut his fight scene. “How do you tell a guy that you’ve cut him out because his sequence is too good?” King says he felt “too young and inexperienced” to complain at the time, but now says he feels “a little p***ed off with it.” Ultimately, though, he sounds philosophical about what happened. The Telegraph article is behind a paywall, but it’s well worth reading if you’re a fan of the original Highlander movie, and want to know more about King’s journey.

There is of course a new Highlander film in the works, starring former Superman actor Henry Cavill in the title role. The pitch is “John Wick with swords.” There’s no release date yet.

items.title: 'All Good Things Come to an End': Doctor Who Writer Believes Show's Return 'Quietly Won't Happen'
items.description: Former Doctor Who writer Mark Gatiss believes the BBC's current plan to reboot the show "quietly won't happen."
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Former Doctor Who writer Mark Gatiss believes the BBC's current plan to reboot the show "quietly won't happen."

Doctor Who is currently off air without a lead actor, showrunner or production team, following the departure of star Ncuti Gatwa, head writer Russell T. Davies and both U.K. maker Bad Wolf and U.S. financial partner Disney. Previous plans to continue the series have now been ditched, with an embarrassing U-turn on the announcement of a one-off episode scheduled for this Christmas.

Officially, the BBC has said it is now putting the rights to produce Doctor Who out to "tender", an official process where it considers bids from various production companies. But it has now been several months since this process was first mentioned, with no obvious further progress towards it actually beginning.

Now, Gatiss has reflected on the fact that the BBC was in a similar situation with Doctor Who before, back at the start of its lengthy hiatus during the 1990s. Then, it took 15 years for the series to fully return.

"The fact that Doctor Who had a second act of 21 years is absolutely amazing," he began, speaking to Radio Times. "And for it to come back possibly even more popular than it was in the first run… but I think maybe it's just time for a break, because all good things come to an end.

"I think the BBC putting it out to tender is a perfectly great idea, but we've been here before. When it was cancelled in 1989 the BBC made a big statement saying 'We're committed to taking Doctor Who through the '90s.' They put it out to tender then, and then it just quietly didn't happen, and I have a feeling maybe that's what's going to happen."

Gatiss concluded by reaffirming that he did not believe Doctor Who was gone forever, but that any expectation its current tender process would prompt a quick return seemed unlikely.

"I feel very doomy, but it's true," he added. "It's fine. I think the fact it's come back so successfully means it will come back again. It's not a one-off 26-year (sic) run, but I think maybe it's just time for a proper break, because you want people to miss it and have fresh ideas, and probably someone to run it who grew up with David Tennant as the Doctor, rather than Tom Baker."

A previous report by Deadline suggested there was now hesitation among production companies to take on Doctor Who, despite — or perhaps because of — its legendary status. "You would have to be mad," one source said. "[It's a] bit of a nightmare for any producer in this market with the shadow of the Disney fallout," said another. A third suggested the series' budget would likely be around $3 million per episode — half of the budget for the episodes Disney previously funded, inviting difficult comparisons.

All of which tallies with comments from former Doctor Who Magazine editor Tom Spilsbury, who last year suggested it would likely be "five or six years before we see anything new," as the series' next incarnation is determined. "At which point, it will be the children of 2005 who will be bringing the show back, just as Russell predicted. As ever, time will tell."

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

A previous report by Deadline suggested there was now hesitation among production companies to take on Doctor Who, despite — or perhaps because of — its legendary status. "You would have to be mad," one source said. "[It's a] bit of a nightmare for any producer in this market with the shadow of the Disney fallout," said another. A third suggested the series' budget would likely be around $3 million per episode — half of the budget for the episodes Disney previously funded, inviting difficult comparisons.

All of which tallies with comments from former Doctor Who Magazine editor Tom Spilsbury, who last year suggested it would likely be "five or six years before we see anything new," as the series' next incarnation is determined. "At which point, it will be the children of 2005 who will be bringing the show back, just as Russell predicted. As ever, time will tell."

items.title: Fast Forever Starts Shooting in December, Confirms Vin Diesel
items.description: The supposedly final chapter in the Fast & Furious saga should begin shooting before the year is out.
items.author: Luke Reilly
items.content:
The Fast & Furious saga’s leading man Vin Diesel has revealed that Fast & Furious 11 – officially known as Fast Forever – will begin shooting this December.

“We start shooting in December, if I can make good on the request from the studio,” Diesel told Variety ahead of a 25th anniversary screening of 2001’s The Fast and the Furious. “I’m in a good place, though. I’ve had to go through four sets of writers, four years of development, to get to something that I felt would be worthy of a finale.”

Diesel shared further details inside the screening itself, noting that after he read the complete script they had “worked so hard to make right,” he was crying.

“I couldn’t hold it back, and I had to tell everyone,” said Diesel. “And my sister said, ‘No more crying, bro.’ So I just want to say that sometimes, even the toughest guys in the world need to cry.”

While a video message from Vin Diesel published in July in costume as Dominic Torreto – and standing in front of the character’s iconic black 1970 Dodge Charger R/T – appeared to suggest production was already officially underway on Fast Forever, it later came to pass that the shoot was related to a World Cup promo that aired in the US during the US vs. Belgium game.

Fast Forever, the long-delayed and supposedly final chapter in the Fast & Furious film saga, is scheduled to hit cinemas on Friday, March 17, 2028. The release date and final title was announced by Universal earlier this year. However, little other information is actually known about the project, which still has no confirmed complete cast yet.

items.title: Avengers: Doomsday Star Sebastian Stan Knows ‘Absolutely Nothing’ About What Happens in the Movie
items.description: Directors Anthony and Joe Russo keeping the complete script from the cast, as with previous Avengers projects.
items.author: Luke Reilly
items.content:
Long-time Marvel Winter Soldier star Sebastian Stan has clarified he knows nothing about the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday, as he worked on the film without ever reading the complete script.

“I know absolutely nothing about it,” said Stan in a newly published French-language interview with French Sunday newspaper Le Journal du Dimanche. “Because we didn’t have a script. We just shot scattered scenes. It’s another way of working, continuously, constantly evolving. The producers didn’t want us to read it in its entirety, to avoid journalists asking us questions. I’ve been following this rule for fifteen years, I’m used to it.”

Stan’s comments came alongside a passing reference to The Batman: Part II being another project he can’t speak about. It’s been subsequently reported Le Journal du Dimanche’s article misquoted Stan making a reference to his role in the film, and the article has since been updated.

It’s worth noting the fact Stan hasn’t seen the complete Avengers: Doomsday script, despite being a part of the film, is actually par for the course when it comes to Marvel’s tentpole ensemble blockbusters.

While specifics vary slightly, it’s been previously reported that only Robert Downey, Jr. and Chris Evans received a full script for Avengers: Infinity War – although Benedict Cumberbatch also noted at the time that he too had read the complete script.

In an oral history of Avengers: Infinity War & Endgame with Rotten Tomatoes, the Russos admitted that only one actor definitely saw the complete script for Endgame: Robert Downey, Jr.

In Stan’s words, being able to participate in projects of such magnitude while still retaining the ability to watch it later as a spectator is part of the “beauty of this job.”

It sounds like he’ll be spectating it alongside a lot of other people, though, with Avengers: Doomsday pre-sale tickets reportedly outpacing Spider-Man: Brand New Day.

items.title: Robin Williams’ Children Revive His Instagram to Fight AI Misuse
items.description: Robin Williams' children Zak, Zelda, and Cody have revived their late father's Instagram account after a decade to combat rampant AI abuse of his voice and likeness.
items.author: Jim Vejvoda
items.content:
Inactive since Robin Williams’ death in 2014, the actor-comedian’s children revived his Instagram account Monday to combat what his daughter Zelda Williams calls “rampant AI abuse of his voice and likeness” on the social media platform.

“As we recognize what would be our Dad's 75th year, we're grateful to see new generations discovering his work while longtime fans continue to celebrate the joy he brought into their lives,” siblings Zak, Zelda and Cody Williams said in the post. “As technology evolves, we want this to be a safe, trusted place where the stories, photos, videos, and memories shared reflect his legacy with authenticity, warmth, and care.”

“This is our way of sharing his unique talent and humor with the world, including the moments that made us and so many of you laugh, as we remember our Dad’s extraordinary life and work. He continues to inspire us and delight people all over the world.”

Zelda Williams commented further on the decision in an Instagram story on her own account.

“I’m sorry if anyone found Dad’s old page posting again to be triggering. Believe me, I know it’s a little strange,” Williams posted. “Making that space into one where people can find authentic clips and photos of him is one of the best ways we’ve now found to fight back against rampant AI abuse of his voice and likeness on here.”

Williams has long made her disdain for AI-generated content of her father known, asking fans in October 2025 to “stop sending me AI videos of Dad.”

“Stop believing I wanna see it or that I’ll understand, I don’t and I won’t. If you’re just trying to troll me, I’ve seen way worse, I’ll restrict and move on,” the actress-director added at the time. “But please, if you’ve got any decency, just stop doing this to him and to me, to everyone even, full stop. It’s dumb, it’s a waste of time and energy, and believe me, it’s not what he’d want.”

Williams previously slammed the “disturbing” use of AI to recreate her father’s voice, bashing such recreations as, “at their very best, a poor facsimile of greater people, but at their worst, a horrendous Frankensteinian monster, cobbled together from the worst bits of everything this industry is, instead of what it should stand for."

Williams’ revulsion at AI recreations of her dad’s voice is not shared by Matthew Lawrence, who played Robin Williams’ son in Mrs. Doubtfire. Lawrence said last year that he would “love” for AI to recreate the actor’s “iconic” voice.

"I would love — now, obviously, with the respect and with the OK from his family — but I would love to do something really special with his voice," Lawrence told Deadline in July 2025, "because I know for a generation, that voice is just so iconic.”

items.title: Call of Duty Socials Accidentally Post Placeholder Marketing Image for Modern Warfare 4, Fans Suspect AI Usage
items.description: The Call of Duty socials team accidentally posted an internal marketing image for Modern Warfare 4, and fans suspect it may be AI-generated.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
The Call of Duty socials team accidentally posted an internal marketing image for Modern Warfare 4, and fans suspect it may be AI-generated.

Earlier today, the Call of Duty Twitter account posted a render of a soldier walking toward the camera while promoting the game's appearance at Gamescom. Eagle-eyed fans examined the image and noticed that the soldier's gun appeared to be warped in an odd way, possibly suggesting the image was AI-generated. The graphic was eventually taken down, and the Call of Duty team stated that it was posted by mistake.

NEW MW4 IMAGE pic.twitter.com/SBIuhXIkYY

— Forward (@ForwardLeaks) August 18, 2026

"Earlier today, an image was mistakenly posted to one of the Call of Duty accounts," said a Call of Duty rep on social media. "It included a temporary render from a marketing style guide. The image was a placeholder and not taken from in-game. We’ve taken it down."

Fans have now begun speculating that Activision has been using AI to generate concepts for marketing material. This probably won't come as a surprise to many Call of Duty fans, as Activision has admitted to using AI to make assets for Call of Duty. On the game's Steam page, there is a disclosure that confirms the usage of generative AI tools to develop assets for the game. Some of these assets include things like calling cards in Black Ops 7.

Following backlash to Black Ops 7's usage of AI in November 2025, Activision issued the following statement: "Like so many around the world, we use a variety of digital tools, including AI tools, to empower and support our teams to create the best gaming experiences possible for our players. Our creative process continues to be led by the talented individuals in our studios."

Nearly a year later, players are still frustrated by Activision's usage of generative AI, with some casting doubt over claims that the artwork was merely a placeholder.

"Activision? Using AI slop for Call of Duty!? Surely there’s been some mistake; they would never," joked one fan. "From a Style guide? How much AI was used in development and art?" asked another fan.

Whether or not there will be any obvious examples of AI-generated content in Modern Warfare 4's beta this weekend remains to be seen. If not, fans will certainly be keeping their eyes open for it when the game launches in October.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.
